checks: The mixed set is a finite union of compact occupied fibers and therefore compact. Taking its hull inside the convex original set gives exactly the same mixed set, even when all fibers are null.

The real base direction space is spanned by integer differences. Its lattice intersection has full relative rank, and a basis identifies exactly the entire affine lattice, including sites not sampled in the original set.
One positive-volume fiber supplies all continuous directions and the occupied base span supplies the independent quotient directions. Consequently the pulled-back canonical hull is full dimensional.

The chart fixes x, so every per-fiber d-volume, including zero, and the counting convention d=0 are unchanged. Halfspace restrictions through corresponding marks either give a reduced halfspace or full mass; every reduced halfspace extends to an ambient one. The infima coincide and r<=n yields the coefficient comparison. The zero-dimensional singleton is handled directly.

Deletes null fibers preserving measure and the maximum, while this theorem keeps them and preserves pointwise marked depths in the full occupied affine span.
